\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دانه} (dâne)}{دانه (dâne)}]{\fa{دانه} (dâne) — a seed, a grain}

\label{lesson:FA-C104-dane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a wave, then the Persian for a root.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دانه}}
\textbf{\fa{دانه}} — \emph{dâne} — \textquotedblleft{}a seed, a grain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dâne} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{dānag}, \textquotedblleft{}grain, seed\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شبنم} (shabnam)}{شبنم (shabnam)}]{\fa{شبنم} (shabnam) — dew}

\label{lesson:FA-C104-shabnam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a storm, then the Persian for fog.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شبنم}}
\textbf{\fa{شبنم}} — \emph{shabnam} — \textquotedblleft{}dew\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shabnam} is \emph{shab}, \textquotedblleft{}night\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{nam}, \textquotedblleft{}moisture\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): the night's moisture. Both parts are native Persian; \emph{shab} is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{šab}.
\end{cousinweb}
